title: Slack vs Microsoft Teams for Remote Teams 2026
description: A workflow-fit guide to Slack and Microsoft Teams. The product profiles classify them under Communication & Collaboration and Communication; the labels overlap but do not prove that the tools are interchangeable. Compare persistent channels, searchable discussions, external guests, live calls, phone features, administration, and how decisions are retained. Choose against your team's actual communication patterns rather than a generic score.

features.name: Free Tier
features.tool1Detail: Slack free limits message history to 90 days
features.tool2Detail: Teams free supports unlimited chat for up to 10 users

features.name: Messaging
features.tool1Detail: Slack has best-in-class threading and channels
features.tool2Detail: Teams messaging is functional but less refined

features.name: Video Calls
features.tool1Detail: Slack Huddles are lightweight and spontaneous
features.tool2Detail: Teams supports larger meetings and webinars

features.name: Integrations
features.tool1Detail: Slack has the largest app ecosystem

features.name: Best For
features.tool1Detail: Slack excels for developer and startup culture
features.tool2Detail: Teams excels for enterprise compliance and Office users

verdict: This comparison does not establish a verified overall winner. Provisional recommendation for remote teams centered on persistent channel conversations and a broad third-party app workflow: start by evaluating Slack. Microsoft Teams may be the better fit when Microsoft 365 integration, meetings, telephony, and centralized enterprise administration are the primary requirements. This is not a verified universal winner; test guest access, search, retention, integrations, security controls, mobile use, and total cost in both products.

faqs.question: Are Slack and Microsoft Teams direct substitutes?
faqs.answer: Not always. Their profiles list overlapping but distinct primary categories (Communication & Collaboration and Communication). Compare the actual communication job and the users involved before treating them as alternatives.

faqs.question: When should I evaluate Slack?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Slack when its core communication workflow matches your team's must-have requirements. Test channels, calls, guest access, search, retention, and administration, and verify current plan limits with the vendor.

faqs.question: When should I evaluate Microsoft Teams?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Microsoft Teams when its core communication workflow matches your requirement. Confirm whether it supports the needed external users, calling or meeting features, integrations, permissions, and data export.

faqs.question: Can the products be used together?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if they cover different communication needs. Verify current integration support and decide which system owns messages, call records, files, and retention so teams do not split important context across disconnected tools.

faqs.question: How should I compare total cost?
faqs.answer: Include user seats, phone numbers or calling usage where applicable, meeting limits, add-ons, storage, administration, integrations, and migration—not just the entry-level subscription.

faqs.question: Does this page name a verified winner?
faqs.answer: No. This is a workflow decision guide, not an independently verified head-to-head score. The stored winner and feature rows are not verified; test your requirements and confirm current details with each vendor.
